The source local arbitrary-join calculation changes join into meet; the actual image/codomain restriction is harmless on the identity witness. Keep original identity on the two-elementpowersetalgebra and subset{bottom,top}:join=top,meet=bottom. Actual FrameHom.id with fullrangeuniv; standard sSup/sInf yieldunequalvalues.

The correct frame-homomorphism law uses ∨₂φ[A], not ∧₂φ[A]. This is exactly preservation of arbitrary joins, which is a defining hypothesis on the frame homomorphism.

fields.problem:
Title: Image of Frame under Frame Homomorphism is Frame/Corollary

Let $L_1 = \struct {S_1, \preceq_1}$ and $L_2 = \struct {S_2, \preceq_2}$ be [[Definition:Frame (Lattice Theory)|frames]].

Let $\phi: S_1 \to S_2$ be a [[Definition:Frame Homomorphism|frame homomorphism]].

Let $L_3 = \struct{S_3, \preceq_3}$ be the [[Definition:Ordered Set|ordered set]] where:
:$S_3$ denotes the [[Definition:Image of Subset under Mapping|image]] of $S_1$ under $\phi$
:$\preceq_3$ denotes the [[Definition:Restricted Ordering|restricted ordering]] of $\preceq_2$ to the [[Definition:Subset|subset]] $S_3$.

Then:

:$\phi \restriction_{S_1 \times S_3 } : \struct {S_1, \preceq_1} \to \struct{S_3, \preceq_3}$ is a [[Definition:Frame Homomorphism|frame homomorphism]]
where:
:$\phi \restriction_{S_1 \times S_3}$ denotes the [[Definition:Restriction of Mapping|restriction]] of the [[Definition:Mapping|mapping]] of $\phi$ to $S_1 \times S_3$
fields.witness: Let S₁=S₂=S₃={0<1}, the two-element frame, and let φ:S₁→S₂ be the identity. Its restriction to S₁×S₃ is unchanged. φ preserves top, finite meets, and all joins, so it is a frame homomorphism. Take A={0,1}. Then ∨₁A=1 and φ[A]={0,1}. The meet of phi[A]={0,1} is 0. Therefore phi(join A)=1 differs from meet phi[A]=0; the displayed local equality fails.

scope_metadata.target_scope: The printed equality phi(join A)=meet phi[A] in the arbitrary-join section; not the theorem that the corestriction to the image is a frame homomorphism.
